extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and advocates submitting comments to the FCC about net neutrality
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for members of the public on drafting and submitting personal comments to the FCC docket about net neutrality (using the DearFCC tool as an example). Emphasizes personalization, concrete personal/community impact, procedural submission through the official docket, and framing the issue in democratic terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized rather than generic templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective comments should be personalized rather than generic templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use original, individual voices — personal testimonies accumulate into significant public pressure. DearFCC helps craft a unique comment using custom-generated text so your submission is not just boilerplate. Avoid copy-pasting stock form letters; unique, specific stories carry more weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe how proposed changes would specifically affect you
rubrics_metrics.description: Address how proposed changes would specifically affect you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie comments to concrete concerns about how ISP throttling or blocking would harm your community's access to information and services. Provide real examples of impacts (e.g., inability to access educational resources, businesses harmed by throttling) rather than abstract policy statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit through the official FCC docket
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments through the official FCC docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural compliance matters — use the official docket so your comment is part of the record. The DearFCC tool is presented as a way to craft a comment and submit it to the official docket with two clicks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect your comment to broader democratic values and policy framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Place your personal testimony within a policy frame that connects to democratic values (e.g., net neutrality as a right to access Internet content freely).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair a clear policy frame (net neutrality protects access to all Internet content from ISP throttling/blocking) with your personal stakes to explain why the issue matters to democracy and civic life. Use the policy definition to contextualize your personal impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid abstract arguments; emphasize real-world stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid abstract arguments — the FCC has heard those; emphasize real-world stakes instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete, specific harms and community effects 'differentiate signal from noise.' Anti-pattern: submitting high-level philosophical or purely technical arguments without linking them to tangible effects on people or services.
